title: Slotless: Switch games on your iPhone and Mac, Switch 2 on the Mac
description: A free Mac app that turns Nintendo Switch games you own into native apps for your iPhone and Mac. No emulator, no account, no terminal. Now with Switch 2 games on the Mac.
hero_title: Your Switch games, on your iPhone and Mac.
hero_sub: Add a game you own, press one button, and play it as a real app. Not an emulator: the game's own code runs directly on the Apple chip. Now Switch 2 games too, on the Mac.
hero_note: No account, no ads, no terminal. Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26.6 or later.
fact2: no price, no subscription, no ads
fact3: the game runs on the chip, not in an emulator
how1: Drag them into the window. They stay on your Mac: nothing is uploaded anywhere.
how2_t: Let the app do the work
how2: It checks your Mac, installs the free tools it needs and builds the game. A first build takes 30 to 60 minutes.
how3: It installs the game on your iPhone over a cable, or makes an app you open on your Mac. It then runs without the Mac's help.
feat_title: Made for people, not only for developers
feat1: The simple mode asks only three things. Commands and logs stay hidden until you ask for them.
feat2: Use a controller, a keyboard you can remap, or touch buttons you can move, resize and hide. A controller is recommended on the iPhone.
feat3: After a build the app offers what it no longer needs. It goes to the Trash, and only if you say so.
feat4: The app speaks English and Russian, and you can switch at any time.
need_sub: Better to know now than after an hour of waiting.
need1: Apple silicon, macOS 26.6 or later, and Xcode 27.2, Apple's free developer app. The app tells you when something is missing.
need2: A game you own and the keys from your own console. Neither comes with this app. A .nup file needs no keys.
need3: About twice the game's size, plus 10 GB, for the first build.
need4: An iPhone 15 Pro or newer, a cable, and Developer Mode turned on.
need5: A free one is enough. Apple then limits you to 3 such apps at a time, and each works for 7 days: reinstall from the app to renew it, and your saves stay.
a1: Yes, all of it. Anyone who wants to may say thanks with a donation, but nothing depends on it.
a2: No. There are no games or keys in the app, on this site or in the project, and we do not link to any. You need your own.
a3: No. This is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo or Apple. Check what your country allows for copies of your own games.
q4: Why does macOS warn me when I open it?
a4: The app is not notarized by Apple. To open it the first time, go to System Settings, then Privacy & Security, and press Open Anyway. The source code is public, so anyone can check what it does.
q5: Why does the game stop after 7 days?
a5: That is Apple's limit for apps signed with a free Apple ID. Connect the iPhone and press Reinstall in the app. A paid developer account lasts a year.
a6: Over 150 games are tested, but some have limits, and others may not start at all. Smaller games are the safest first try on an iPhone.
a7: They stay on your Mac. The app downloads its own components from GitHub and developer tools from their usual sources, and uploads nothing of yours.
support_title: Free for everyone. Thanks are welcome.
support_sub: If this saved your evening, you can support the work with a donation of any size. It stays free either way.
legal: Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo. iPhone and Mac are trademarks of Apple. This project is not affiliated with them. Use it only with games and keys you own.
credits: Open source, MIT license. Built on
vs_title: Why it plays like a real app
vs_emu_note: Something has to imitate the console for as long as you play.
vs_nat_note: The game's own code runs on the chip, changed only where Apple's system requires it. A small host answers the game's system calls, and its NVN, Vulkan and OpenGL graphics are drawn through Metal.
pick_label: Where do you want to play?
need_mac: The game becomes an app on this Mac. No cable and no 7-day limit from Apple.
demo_hint: Drag the buttons, change their size, or hide them. It works like this inside a game on the iPhone.
shot_build: While it works: plain steps, the time left, and a way to cancel.
shot_ready_alt: The app's window: a game, keys, Mac selected as where to play, and a Build for Mac button
shot_build_alt: The app's window during a build: step 3 of 7 with a progress bar and a list of finished steps
shot_note: Real windows of the app. The game name, sizes and times in them are an example.

hero_new: ★ New: Switch 2 games, native on the Mac
a8: Yes, on the Mac, as of version 0.7. Eleven are in the games list, among them Mario Kart World and Donkey Kong Bananza. The iPhone is untested. Use your own game as one .nup file, which needs no keys. These games are demanding: Ocarina of Time alone takes about 11 GB of memory, so a Mac with 8 GB will struggle.
sw2_title: Switch 2 is here. Native. No emulator.
sw2_lede: The games of Nintendo's newest console now become real Mac apps. Their code runs right on the Apple chip, and their NVN2 graphics and shaders are rebuilt for Metal. One file in, one app out.
sw2_note: Mac only for now: the iPhone is untested. You need your own copy of the game. These games are demanding: Ocarina of Time alone takes about 11 GB of memory, so a Mac with 8 GB will struggle.
